predecessors.name: Kingdom of Denmark
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Estonia (Harria and Vironia, Reval), which 'became split' between a pro-Danish and a pro-German party after the king's death

successors.name: Teutonic Order
successors.text: Estonia (Harria and Vironia), sold for 19,000 Cologne marks; sovereignty shifted on 1 November 1346

successors.name: Kingdom of Denmark
successors.text: the southern Jutland land, back with the kingdom

ledger.x: 2 August 1332: Christopher II dies and the Danish crown's lands pass to mortgagees.
16 May 1343: the Order takes the castles of Reval and Wesenberg.
1 November 1346: the contest ends with the sale.
1 November 1346: Denmark's king sells Estonia to the Teutonic Order.
1351: Cliopatria's last Danish Magnates shape ends.

wars.name: Danish interregnum (mortgagees)
wars.outcome: 'Upon his death Denmark ceased being a formal kingdom, and for the next eight years it was subdued by various mortgagees': Count Gerhard took Jutland and Count Johan Funen and Zealand 'as his personal property' (undated).

wars.name: St George's Night Uprising
wars.outcome: After the rising of 1343 the Order took the castles of Reval and Wesenberg (16 May 1343) and Narva (1345); Denmark sold Estonia to the Order in 1346.

certainty.note: The Estonian province's inland frontier and the southern Jutland sliver are approximate; the Treaty of Stensby (7 June 1238) had fixed Harria and Vironia as the king's duchy.
